text.p: Julen Guerrero struck a first-half hat-trick to take Spain to the top of their World Cup qualifying group with a 3-0 win over Malta in which both sides finished with 10 men.
Guerrero scored in the eighth, 26th and 33rd minutes as Spain's skill and speed overwhelmed a young and inexperienced Maltese side in the Ta'Qali stadium.
But Malta fought back as the game wore on and Spain were unable to add to their score.

Malta defender Darren Debono was sent off in the 70th minute for a second bookable offence. Soon afterwards Spain's substitute Guillermo Amor also received his marching orders for his second yellow card offence.
Guerrero profited from a defensive blunder to score his first goal and netted the second from a cross by Guardiola after Juan Antonio Pizzi had headed against the post.
Guardiola provided a stream of passes throughout the match and from another of these Guerrero claimed his third goal.
Pizzi had a header cleared off the line in the 55th minute.
Spain overtook Yugoslavia to lead European group six by one point with 13 points from five games. Malta are bottom after conceding 21 goals in their four group defeats so far.
Malta - Reginald Cini, Joseph Brincat, Richard Buhaglar, Jeffrey Chetcuti, Darren Debono, Hubert Suda, Noel Turner, Antoine Zahra, Ivan Zammit, Gilbert Aglus, Aldrin Muscat.

Spain - Andoni Zubizarreta, Armando Alvarez, Alberto Belsue, Miquel Angel Nadal, Roberto Rios, Josep Guardiola (Gullermo Amor), Julen Guerrero, Luis Enrique, Fernando Herro, Raul Gonzalez, Juan Antonio Pizzi.
